summary.headline: Supriya Lifescience Q4 FY26 revenue rose 50% YoY to INR277 crore (record quarter); FY26 revenue INR828 crore, EBITDA margin 35.5%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue of INR277 crore grew 50% YoY, with EBITDA of INR98 crore (35.5% margin) and PAT of INR74 crore. FY26 revenue grew 19% to INR828 crore, in line with the ~20% guidance, while EBITDA rose 13% to INR294 crore as margin reached 35.5%, above the 33-35% guided range. Management cited an INR10 crore hit to Q4 revenue from geopolitical supply-chain disruption, crude and solvent price spikes and shortages. The Lote USFDA surprise inspection ended with a Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI) classification and one minor observation. Management reiterated the INR1,000 crore FY27 revenue target, with a planned August shutdown making quarterly growth non-linear.

segments.name: Export / regulated markets
segments.commentary: Exports were 82% of FY26 revenue; Europe grew strongly, helped by CEP approvals for two to three products and new customers on existing CEP products. Asia and semi-regulated markets grew on launches of three products last year.

segments.name: Cardiovascular advanced intermediate
segments.commentary: Launched in Q3 FY26 and contributed from Q4. Management expects about 300 metric tons of capacity to be near full utilisation in FY27, with the full volume over 2-3 years, and has lock-in with three or four large customers.

segments.name: Anesthetics (incl. liquid anesthetic)
segments.commentary: Portfolio has six to seven products and is among the fastest-growing in regulated markets. Liquid anesthetic was commercialised in FY26 with 1,000+ MT capacity at Lote; CMO discussion is at an advanced stage with no term sheet yet.

segments.name: DSM contract (CDMO/vitamins, Riboflavin)
segments.commentary: Running at about 3 tons a month; contributed INR30-35 crore in FY26, with a peak of about INR60 crore expected in FY27.

segments.name: ADHD product
segments.commentary: Launched in FY26 with strong demand in LATAM and Europe; more growth expected over coming quarters.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR1,000 crore, described as firmly on track; growth will not be linear because of the August annual maintenance shutdown for older blocks A and D.
Revenue growth of ~20% annually and EBITDA margin of 33-35% reiterated; management said the margin band will hold for the next 5-6 years given the semi-regulated launch cycle.
Planned launch of 3-4 products a year, including about 2 new anesthetic and 2 new ADHD launches in FY27.
Contrast media launch pushed to H2 FY27.
Effective tax rate for FY27 about 25.17%.
Working capital days target of 170-180 days.
GLP-1 development: no agreement signed yet; revenue at least 2 years away.
Protein (weight-loss related) technology: no large revenue expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: Patalganga land has all clearances; Phase 1 (about INR200 crore, two API/advanced intermediate blocks and two formulation blocks) groundbreaking in FY27.
F block at Lote: adds 150-200 KL capacity over about 2 years, with capex of INR40-50 crore; includes debottlenecking and a D block extension.
Capacity utilisation cited at about 76%; the Q2 FY27 shutdown is for debottlenecking and refurbishment.
Ambernath finished-formulation facility: expenses have started but revenue is small; EU audit expected in H2 FY27 (around Oct-Nov); USFDA audit date not yet given. Full revenue effect 3-4 years away.
Liquid anesthetic formulation approval: no European audit date yet; finished-formulation ramp is 3-4 years away, so FY27 revenue comes from API at Lote.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 revenue hit by about INR10 crore from supply-chain disruption, crude and solvent price spikes and shortages.
Management said pricing pressure is not significant: raw material increases were passed through on purchase-order-based contracts.
US exposure is limited for the current portfolio; Europe and LATAM are the larger markets. US share should rise over 3-4 years with the anesthetic and ADHD launches.
R&D focus: niche APIs, CMO/CDMO/CRO tie-ups, and Ambernath finished formulations in liquid, aesthetics and injectables. R&D spend has roughly doubled over three years.
Contrast media: a process-cost advantage was claimed; management does not aim for more than 40-50% market share.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 300 MT cardiovascular intermediate order converted, and what is its regulatory and PLI status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said scale-up started in Q4 and it expects about 300 MT to be near full utilisation in FY27. Three or four large customers have been locked in. The company has not joined any PLI scheme and does not intend to.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance not consistent with this single product's potential?
qa_highlights.answer: The full 300 MT volume will take 2-3 years; FY27 guidance does not include the full product potential. Management said core therapeutic categories are not degrowing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the US market small for Supriya despite USFDA approval?
qa_highlights.answer: The current portfolio's larger markets are Europe and LATAM because most finished-dosage formulators are there. New anesthetic and ADHD launches are expected to raise US exposure over 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital days and inventory days rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said backward integration requires higher inventory, and the cardiovascular and liquid anesthetic intermediates are large. Ambernath adds INR10-15 crore of inventory. Receivables rose to 78 days, mainly from the last two months; management expects 80-85 days at worst.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q4 run-rate of about INR270 crore be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined quarter-on-quarter run-rate guidance. It reiterated INR1,000 crore for FY27, with the Q2 shutdown making quarters non-linear.

risks_watch: Ambernath USFDA and EU audit timing is unconfirmed (EU audit H2 FY27); delay pushes out finished-formulation revenue.
Liquid anesthetic formulation approval in Europe is not yet scheduled, so FY27 revenue comes from API only.
Working capital: receivable days (78) and inventory days (near 200) rising; the 170-180 day target depends on Ambernath ramp.
Q2 FY27 shutdown and the 150-200 KL capacity addition are the swing factors for FY27 quarterly and INR1,000 crore revenue.
Raw material and solvent cost pressure from crude and geopolitical disruption; pass-through depends on customer acceptance.
Margin of 33-35% depends on the mix shifting to regulated markets as semi-regulated launches mature over 2-3 years.
Contrast media launch slipped to H2 FY27 and has no date yet; GLP-1 and protein deals are still at discussion stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, the FY27 INR1,000 crore target and margin band, and on regulatory progress. Management was evasive on specifics: product pricing, the quantity of the cardiovascular order, CMO terms, Ambernath and Patalganga revenue potential, and gross margin, citing confidentiality until contracts are signed.
key_quotes: Our Lote facility had received the USFDA's Establishment Inspection Report, EIR, with a Voluntary Action Indicated classification following the surprise inspection conducted in February 2026.
We iterate our guidance of approximately 20% annual growth revenue and EBITDA margin, 33% to 35%.
So, all quarters might not be linear growth, because like our Chairman said already that in the quarter 2, we are expecting some shutdown and some refurbishing activities.

growth.why: Management reiterates ~20% annual revenue growth and the INR1,000 crore FY27 target (implies ~21% over FY26's INR828 crore), backed by commissioned cardiovascular and liquid anesthetic capacity, DSM riboflavin peak (~INR60 crore) and 3-4 launches a year, though the FY27 path is non-linear due to the August shutdown and the Patalganga INR200 crore capex only starts in FY27.
